content.text: BAMS, also known as Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery, is a trending medical science course in India where students gain hands-on experience in Ayurveda. It is a 5.5-year undergraduate course, including a year for an internship. BAMS admission in Karnataka is conducted by several institutions. Both private and government colleges are among them. Students who want to pursue BAMS in Karnataka must follow this article minutely. Here we are going to discuss in detail the best colleges in the state, their admission procedure, the eligibility criteria, and fees. Remember, for admission, NEET is mandatory, just like all the other states in India.

sections.heading: BAMS Admission in Karnataka Overview

content.text: All admissions to the BAMS course are conducted by the Karnataka BAMS counselling , where the students can apply to different colleges in the state depending on their scores in the NEET examination.
In total, 82 colleges provide BAMS admission in Karnataka, including both private and government ones.

items: According to NCISM, there are nearly 800-900 BAMS seats available in the government colleges of Karnataka.
And for the private colleges, there are approximately 5000+ seats.

content.text: The Karnataka Examination Authority (KEA) conducts the Ayush Counselling in Karnataka, where state-domicile students and students from other states can participate in the State Quota and All India Quota, respectively.

sections.heading: BAMS Eligibility in Karnataka

content.text: Candidates mandatorily need to qualify the National Eligiblity cum Entrance Test (NEET) for BAMS admission in Karnataka. The NEET-qualified students can only participate in the AYUSH counselling. This ensures the students get AIQ seats or State quota seats, according to the domicile of the candidates and preference of the college. The students who want to pursue BAMS admission are required to follow the BAMS eligibility in Karnataka.
Entrance Exam : The National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET UG)
Academic Qualification:

items: Must pass the 10+2 board examination from a recognised board.
Should have 12th in the science stream with subjects Physics, Chemistry, and Biology/Biochemistry.

Candidates need to score a minimum of 50% aggregate in their 12th examination in the Physics, Chemistry, and Biology subjects. There is a relaxation of marks for the reserved candidates (Minimum 40% aggregate for SC/ST students).

content.text: Age Limit:

items: Students must be over 17 years old in the year of admission.

sections.heading: BAMS Admission Process in Karnataka

content.text: The admission procedure of BAMS includes NEET counselling. Ayush Admissions Central Counseling Committee (AACCC) conducts all the BAMS admissions in India. And in the state of Karnataka, counselling is conducted by KEA under the supervision of the Ministry of Ayush. Below is a step-by-step guideline for BAMS admission in Karnataka. Follow them for a smooth admission procedure.
Step 1: Visit the official website of KEA and input all your personal required information and NEET UG roll no on the portal.
Step 2: Make payment of the counselling fees after uploading all the relevant original documents and submit the form.

Step 3: The candidates are allowed to in their preferences through the choice filling round. In this round, they can select the colleges in Karnataka from the available list according to their preference.

Step 4: The seat allotment list will be published by the KEA after the end date of the counselling. Remember, the seat allotment is done based on NEET rank, category, seat availability, and preference.
Step 5: Upon seat allotment, pay the college fees and download the KEA admission order. This order is mandatory for reporting to the college.

Step 6: Lastly, report to your college. Carry all the necessary documents that are pre-mentioned by the college. Bring both originals and photocopies along with you to complete the document verification.

sections.heading: Documents Required for BAMS Admission in Karnataka

content.text: Below is the list of documents that are required for BAMS admission in Karnataka. The set-listed documents must be produced at the time of document verification upon reporting to the college. Carry 2 or 3 photocopies of the documents in case of any inconvenience.

items: KEA admission order.
The Allotment Letter
The NEET Admit Card
The NEET Score Card
Class 10th & 12th Passing Certificate
Class 10th & 12th Marksheet
Transfer Certificate
Medical Fitness Certificate
Any government-approved Identity Proof (Aadhar/PAN Card/Driving License/ Voter ID, Passport)
Passport-size photos
Caste Certificate (If applicable)
Domicile Certificate (If applicable)
Income Certificate (If applicable)
Disability Certificate (If applicable)

sections.heading: BAMS Fees in Karnataka

content.text: The Ministry of AYUSH and the government of India have jointly agreed on the state governments’ independence to provide the BAMS course with their own selective fee structure. So, the private and government colleges all over Karnataka have different course fees for admission.

While the government colleges generally take low admission fees, the private ones charge a little extra with the promise to provide the best infrastructure and faculty. To get a detailed fee structure, it is recommended to visit the official websites of the colleges. Here are the average fees for private and government BAMS colleges in Karnataka.

sections.heading: BAMS Careers in Karnataka

content.text: BAMS graduates can secure both private and government jobs in the state. There are plenty of Govt jobs for BAMS doctors in Karnataka. The average annual salary for an Ayurvedic doctor in India ranges from INR 3,60,000/- to INR 7,20,000/-. BAMS graduates in Karnataka have a range of career opportunities. They get jobs in government hospitals, private clinics, wellness centres, and Ayurvedic pharmaceutical companies. Even after completion of the BAMS course, they can also pursue roles in research institutions or academia. Students can choose to pursue higher studies after the BAMS course, too.
